speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a low-grade fever, an itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics. To understand what is happening, were you being treated for a specific infection, such as strep throat or pneumonia, before developing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-Induced Erythema Multiforme. The clinical presentation of fever, generalized joint pain, and a rash that began in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and extremities is highly characteristic of erythema multiforme following amoxicillin treatment for sinusitis.
